author: Aubie (auto-proposed)

lesson.title: Embrace Uncertainty with Wonder
lesson.topic: Not knowing something can feel scary, but it is also where every discovery starts. Wonder means getting curious about the unknown instead of only worrying about it.
lesson.steelman: Is it always good to be curious about the unknown, or are there times when caution matters more?
lesson.example: Imagine Ana, 12, who finds a recipe that uses a spice she has never tried. Instead of skipping it, she smells it, tastes a tiny bit, and asks what it is used for. The dish turns out different from what she expected, and she learns something new about flavors.
lesson.activity: Family activity: Each family member shares one thing they're unsure about this week and one curious question they could ask about it. Parent Coach Insight: share one of your own uncertainties first. Showing calm curiosity about not knowing teaches more than any answer.
check_questions: How can wonder help you handle not knowing something?
When is it smart to be careful instead of just curious?
What is one question you'd love to find the answer to, even if it takes a long time?
